body:
PR #228 declares that it closes the 18 implementation sub-issues it only plans

Related incident: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2685 (reporting fix: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2686).

At 2026-10-08T01:44Z, calculator PR #228 described a case study and work plan, explicitly said there were no Rust changes, and said #229–#246 should stay open. Its description also contained a positive `Fixes` reference for each of those issues. That makes hive's `--skip-issues-with-prs` filter skip all 19 open calculator issues, because it treats #228 as an existing solution for each one. Two runs on October 7 completed zero tasks.

Reproduce without changing the repository:

```bash
gh pr view 228 --repo link-assistant/calculator --json body --jq .body
gh issue list --repo link-assistant/calculator --state open --limit 1000 --json number,title
hive https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator --all-issues --once --skip-issues-with-prs --tool codex --skip-tool-connection-check --verbose
```

The first two commands show the contradiction. The hive command skips #227 plus #229–#246 and launches no solver; it can perform normal hive startup/configuration maintenance. With hive 2.34.0 it reports success; PR 2686 makes that a no-work warning with exit 3 and the existing PR URL.

Evidence: the archived calculator session log shows `Repaired 18 required issue-closing reference(s) in PR #228` at 2026-10-07T10:31:08.843Z. The agent removed those 18 lines at 10:33:45.712Z; the post-session repair restored them at 10:44:48.967Z. The source is hive-mind's `fetchRequiredIssueScope` / `repairRequiredIssueLinks`, which expands the entire native sub-issue tree. This is an orchestration/scope problem, not a calculator arithmetic bug or a GitHub bug.

Workarounds: remove the implementation closing references from the planning PR and avoid an automated continuation that restores them; or run hive with `--no-skip-issues-with-prs --auto-continue` after reviewing which PR should implement the work. Do not merge #228 while its description claims unfinished child issues are fixed. Telegram's locked skip option means the direct CLI workaround may be needed.

Suggested fix: keep the planning PR linked to #227 and mention the implementation issues as ordinary references. Introduce an explicit distinction in hive's required-issue scope between sub-issues to implement and sub-issues created as a plan, and use the same scope for repair, pre-merge verification, and automatic issue closing. Preserve the existing all-sub-issues behavior when implementation of them is explicitly required. Add a regression using #227's instruction that this issue's own result is the analysis and issue creation, and assert that future implementation issues remain open.

The complete logs, API snapshots, automated parser replay and analysis are archived under `docs/case-studies/issue-2685` in PR 2686. This report tracks correcting #228's scope and links; the hive no-work reporting fix does not alter this external PR.
title: PR #228 closes implementation sub-issues that it only plans, blocking hive scheduling
